drivingQuestion: Why is R' Yosei's view stated separately?

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּךְ וְכוּ׳. הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא! הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְכׇל הָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר בְּשֵׁם אוֹמְרוֹ מֵבִיא גְּאוּלָּה לָעוֹלָם.
segments.en: § The mishna states that «Rabbi Yosei says: Neither» in «this» sense, as the blood of a menstruating woman according to Akavya ben Mahalalel, nor in that sense, as a liquid that renders food susceptible according to Rabbi Meir, is green blood considered blood. The Gemara raises a difficulty: «Isn’t this» the same as the opinion of «the first tanna?» The Gemara answers that «this» is what the mishna «is teaching us: Who is the first tanna? Rabbi Yosei. And» the reason Rabbi Yosei’s name is mentioned is due to the principle that «anyone who reports a statement in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world.»
